title: Velocity-time graphs
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:40Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point teaches the signed-area link for Specialist Maths: the closest, mat-reading-motion-from-graphs, covers the gradient and direction ideas but not area as displacement, and phys-motion-graphs is at Physics depth and gives unsigned area.

draft.title: Velocity-time graphs
card: A velocity-time graph plots velocity v on the vertical axis against time t. The gradient at a point is the acceleration at that time.
The signed area between the graph and the t-axis is the change in position, called displacement. Area above the axis counts as positive. Area below counts as negative.
Distance travelled adds up all the areas as positive numbers. Displacement keeps the signs.
Example: v = 4 m/s from t = 0 to t = 3, then v = −2 m/s from t = 3 to t = 7. Displacement = 4×3 + (−2)×4 = 12 − 8 = 4 m. Distance = 12 + 8 = 20 m.
draft.remember: Gradient gives acceleration. Signed area gives displacement.

a.q: A particle has v = 5 m/s from t = 0 to t = 2, then v = −3 m/s from t = 2 to t = 6. What is its displacement from t = 0 to t = 6?
a.why: Displacement = 5×2 + (−3)×4 = 10 − 12 = −2 m. The tempting answer 22 m is the distance, which treats the negative area as positive.
a.clue: Area below the t-axis counts as negative.

b.q: Priya's cycle has velocity rising in a straight line from 2 m/s at t = 0 to 10 m/s at t = 4 seconds. What is her acceleration, and how far does she travel in that time?
b.why: Gradient = (10 − 2) ÷ 4 = 2 m/s². The area is a trapezium: ½ × (2 + 10) × 4 = 24 m. The option 40 m uses the final velocity 10 × 4, which ignores that she started at 2 m/s.
b.clue: Gradient is rise over run. The area is a trapezium.
